title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Rules on Escorting by Judicial Police of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Rules for Escorting by Judicial Police of People's Courts

Fa Fa [2003] No. 19

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

The Rules for Escorting by Judicial Police of People's Courts are hereby issued to you. Please organize study, implementation, and enforcement carefully. If any problems arise during enforcement, please report them to this Court in a timely manner.

November 3, 2003

Rules for Escorting by Judicial Police of People's Courts

Article 1 These Rules are formulated to standardize the escorting work of judicial police of people's courts and to ensure the smooth progress of criminal trials in people's courts, in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China, the Interim Regulations on Judicial Police of People's Courts, and other relevant laws and regulations.

Article 2 Escorting refers to the official act of judicial police of people's courts, during criminal trial activities, to forcibly escort a defendant from a detention center or other custodial facility to the court to stand trial and then return the defendant to the detention center or other custodial facility after the trial, in order to ensure the smooth conduct of the trial. Escorting consists of three processes: escorted transfer to the court, escorting within the courtroom, and escorted transfer back to custody.

Article 3 When judicial police perform escorting duties:

(1) They must possess valid credentials and relevant documents proving their identity.

(2) They shall dress in uniform as prescribed, maintain a neat and dignified police appearance, and conduct themselves with decorum.

(3) They shall be equipped with police implements and weapons in accordance with the Regulations of the People's Police on the Use of Police Implements and Weapons.

(4) One defendant shall be escorted by two judicial police officers; for a defendant in a major case, the defendant shall be escorted by three judicial police officers; a female defendant shall be escorted by female judicial police officers.

Article 4 Judicial police performing escorting duties shall possess good physical and psychological qualities, as well as the necessary adaptability and prevention capabilities, and shall undergo regular specialized training in escorting skills.

Article 5 The work of escorted transfer to the court shall be organized and implemented by the judicial police department. Before the escorted transfer begins, the following preparations shall be made in advance:

(1) Conduct on-site surveys of the temporary custodial location for the defendant, the vehicle access route, the route for the defendant to enter and leave the courtroom, the standing position, and the security posts outside the courtroom, and formulate a specific implementation plan.

(2) Determine the escorting police force based on the circumstances of the case and the number of defendants.

(3) Coordinate with relevant departments to clarify responsibilities.

(4) Determine the division of labor and collaboration plan for judicial police.

(5) Formulate measures for handling emergency situations.

(6) Inspect police equipment such as dedicated prison vans, police implements, weapons, and communication devices.

(7) Select judicial police to serve as full-time drivers.

Article 6 When judicial police perform an escorted transfer to the court:

(1) They shall strictly comply with the relevant rules and regulations of the detention center or other custodial facility, verify one by one the defendant's name, age, cause of action, and other identity elements, and conduct a body search of the defendant to prevent the carrying of dangerous items. When escorting the defendant from custody, restraint devices shall be used on the defendant.

(2) Co-defendants, adult defendants and minor defendants, male defendants and female defendants, and other defendants who are unsuitable to ride in the same vehicle shall be transferred to the court in separate vehicles; for defendants in major cases, one vehicle per person shall be ensured.

(3) Carefully plan the driving route; when multiple prison vans are performing escort transfer tasks, they shall travel in formation; when two or more prison vans are escorting defendants, a command vehicle shall be provided, and a backup vehicle shall be provided if necessary; no person unrelated to the escort work shall ride in the dedicated prison van.

Article 7 Before judicial police perform escorting within the courtroom, they shall focus on making the following preparations:

(1) Understand the identity and number of defendants in this case and other relevant circumstances.

(2) Know the order in which defendants will appear in court and the time of their appearance.

(3) Inspect restraint devices and firearms.

(4) For defendants who are likely to cause a disturbance in court, attempt to escape, commit suicide, or self-harm, preventive measures shall be taken.

Article 8 When judicial police perform escorting within the courtroom:

(1) They shall perform the duties of escorting within the courtroom in accordance with the instructions of the presiding judge or the single judge.

(2) They shall observe courtroom discipline, remain focused, and maintain a serious attitude. They shall not allow unrelated persons to contact the defendant; they shall not converse with the defendant or inquire about the case at will; they shall not insult or covertly physically punish the defendant; they shall not engage in acts that obstruct trial activities, such as urging the trial personnel to shorten the trial time.

(3) Generally, restraint devices shall not be used on the defendant during courtroom proceedings. For the trial of a defendant in a major case, restraint devices may be used based on security needs; for minor defendants, restraint devices shall never be used.

(4) When bringing the defendant into the courtroom, the judicial police shall stand at the side and slightly behind the defendant, hold the defendant's elbow, and maintain a standard pace. They shall bring the defendant to the designated position, facing the trial personnel to stand. After the presiding judge or single judge instructs, "Please remove the defendant's restraint devices," they shall immediately remove the defendant's restraint devices.

(5) Adopt a standing or sitting posture depending on the circumstances: before the prosecutor finishes reading the indictment and during the court pronouncement of judgment, the judicial police shall adopt a standing posture, standing on the side and slightly behind the defendant, holding the defendant's elbow with one hand, with the other hand hanging naturally, heels together and aligned, legs straight, and chest naturally out; at other times, the judicial police may adopt a sitting posture, sitting on the side and slightly behind the defendant, with the upper body straight, arms placed on the thighs or chair armrests, and legs apart at shoulder width.

(6) When three judicial police officers escort a defendant in a major case, they shall always adopt a standing posture. Among them, two judicial police officers shall stand on each side and slightly behind the defendant, holding the defendant's elbow with one hand, with the other hand hanging naturally; the other judicial police officer shall stand behind the defendant, maintaining an attention position.

Article 9 When a case is being tried in court, judicial police shall closely observe the defendant's movements. If the defendant causes a disturbance in court, commits assault, riots, escapes, or similar situations, they shall make every effort to subdue or apprehend the defendant, and may use police implements and weapons in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulations of the People's Police on the Use of Police Implements and Weapons. If unexpected situations such as disturbances or riots occur in the spectator gallery, they shall strictly control the defendant, strictly perform the functions of courtroom escort, and shall not leave their posts without authorization.

Article 10 After the court is adjourned or the trial is closed, when judicial police perform the escorted transfer back to custody:

(1) They shall put restraint devices on the defendant. If the public gathers to watch, judicial police shall strictly control the defendant and reasonably organize security.

(2) When judicial police escort the defendant back to the detention center or other custodial facility, they shall again verify the identity and number of the defendant, properly handle registration and handover procedures, to avoid errors.

(3) Other work rules for the escorted transfer back to custody shall be implemented by reference to the relevant provisions on escorted transfer to the court in these Rules.

Article 11 If judicial police violate these Rules when performing escorting, they shall be dealt with in accordance with the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 12 These Rules shall take effect on the date of promulgation.
